name: Fast Controlled Generation with Adaptive Weighted Rejection Sampling
executive_summary: Enforce output constraints via rejection sampling with adaptively weighted proposals, trading the finite-state-machine indexing approach for a sampling-based alternative that can be faster in some regimes.
description: An alternative family to index-based grammar-constrained decoding: propose candidate continuations from the unconstrained model, weight proposals adaptively based on how likely they are to satisfy the constraint, and reject-and-resample when a proposal fails. Useful when building a full constrained-decoding index (as in structured-output-json-mode) is impractical for the constraint at hand.
when_to_use: The constraint is difficult to compile into an efficient finite-state index, or a lighter-weight/library-free approach is preferred.
when_not_to_use: A well-supported finite-state-index implementation (e.g. structured-output-json-mode) is already available for the constraint type.
known_pitfalls: Rejection sampling efficiency degrades if the constraint is very restrictive relative to the unconstrained model's proposal distribution — most proposals get rejected.
